mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate indicates tight monetary conditions, which can lead to decreased corporate borrowing and investment, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If high FEDFUNDS does not correlate with negative 20-day S&P 500 returns in over 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in unemployment rate below 5% signals a strong labor market, potentially leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE below 5% does not result in positive 20-day returns more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment alongside rising retail sales indicates strong demand, which can boost corporate revenues and drive positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both PAYEMS and RSAFS increases do not correlate with positive 60-day returns in over 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 120 indicates strong supply activity, which may lead to increased economic output and positive S&P 500 returns, especially during an expansion.
failure_condition: If INDPRO above 120 during expansion does not result in positive 60-day returns more than 60% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand in the housing market, which can lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases do not correlate with positive 20-day returns in over 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 4% may indicate tight monetary policy, leading to decreased investment and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS above 4% does not result in negative 20-day returns more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth combined with low unemployment indicates a strong economy, which can lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth and UNRATE decrease do not correlate with positive 60-day returns in over 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales growth exceeding 5% may indicate strong consumer demand, which can lead to increased revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days during economic expansion.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth above 5% during expansion does not result in positive 60-day returns more than 60% of the time.
